newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by slow pork sales and light packer demand, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.
USDA said fresh retail pork cuts were untested at midday in its central U.S. carlot pork report. There were 18.0 loads of pork cuts and 3.0 loads of trimmed, processed pork sold.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to plants were seen steady-$0.50 lower at $59.50 to $60.00 and Illinois tops were expected steady at $58.50 to $59.00.
But Illinois prices could be buoyed by strong packer demand, sources there said. The firm regional demand was seen furthered by light hog movement in central Illinois.
"There weren't that many offered today," a central Illinois buyer said.
Indiana/Ohio hogs at plant were seen trading at a top of $59.00 to $59.50, sources in those areas said.

Despite bearish-looking fundamentals including recent weak wholesale pork prices and packers' cutbacks in hog slaughter, CME traders said they expect cash hog prices to be steady to $0.50 higher on Tuesday amid relatively light hog marketings.
